stories.title: When it came to Cal AI’s viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
stories.simple_summary: A company called Cal AI became popular through paid social media influencers. It made $30 million in two years before being bought by MyFitnessPal.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and business people looking at how companies grow. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
stories.simple_summary: ChatGPT's helper tool for the Chrome web browser can now look at the other websites you have open. You have to give it permission by tagging Chrome when you use it.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT and have the Chrome extension installed, it might be easier to ask ChatGPT questions about your open websites, but it also means ChatGPT can see what you're looking at.

stories.title: Sega pulls Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale following disastrous launch
stories.simple_summary: A video game company released a fixed-up old game but had to stop selling it because it was full of bugs. The company also used AI to make the old graphics look newer, which didn't work well.
stories.why_it_matters: If you bought this game, you might want a refund. Otherwise this is mainly a story about one company's bad launch.

stories.title: The tech backlash is now in theaters
stories.simple_summary: Several movies coming out in 2026 are criticizing big tech companies and their leaders. These films show a more negative view of how Silicon Valley is changing society.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't really affect your daily life. It's just entertainment taking a harder look at the tech world.

stories.title: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work
stories.simple_summary: President Trump posted photos of White House work on social media, but one photo appears to have been changed using AI to look better. An AI detector caught the changes.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect you directly, but it shows that AI-edited images are getting more common and that even important people are using them.

stories.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
stories.simple_summary: Meta and Apple partnered to create an AI tool called Muse Spark Open that can work on Apple computers. It's an AI model that runs on your own computer instead of somewhere else online.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a Mac, this might let you use powerful AI tools without sending your information to the internet. This mostly matters to people who care about privacy or need advanced AI on their computer.

stories.title: Bluesky’s AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social
stories.simple_summary: Bluesky's AI tool now helps you create simple games, polls, and dashboards that you can share with other people. It's a way to build things without knowing how to code.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're interested in making simple games or interactive tools to share with friends, this makes it easier. Most people won't need this.

stories.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps
stories.simple_summary: Amazon's leader says he thinks future AI devices will work quietly in the background and guess what you need. Instead of you telling a device what to do, it will do things before you ask.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about a future idea, not something available now. It's mostly for tech watchers to think about.

stories.title: Anthropic is letting METR researchers look under the hood with employee-level access
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, a company that makes AI, is letting outside researchers look at how it works and find problems. The company promises not to block what these researchers publish.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to people who care about AI safety. It shows one company trying to be more open about how it works.

stories.title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more
stories.simple_summary: Bluesky's Attie platform now lets people create websites, games, and quizzes without knowing how to write computer code. These things can connect to the Bluesky social network.
stories.why_it_matters: If you want to make simple interactive tools to share, this makes it possible. Most small business owners won't need this feature.

stories.title: Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs
stories.simple_summary: Meta created a powerful AI model called Muse Spark Open that works on expensive Apple computers. It's made to run well on Mac devices.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech companies and people with very powerful computers. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Last chance to save up to $200 on your TechCrunch Founder Summit pass: Early booking ends October 16
stories.simple_summary: This is an advertisement for a business conference in Boston on November 4. Early ticket discounts end October 16.
stories.why_it_matters: This only matters if you're a business founder or investor who wants to attend a conference. Most people can skip this.
